mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a key driver of equity valuations; lower rates compress discount rates and boost equity prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of the periods when HOUST < 1300.0.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) rises above 4.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods when UNRATE > 4.5 AND INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) signals a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 index units signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer spending (RSAFS) is above 450000 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.5%, it signals strong consumer demand and accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods when RSAFS > 450000.0 AND FEDFUNDS < 0.5.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units signals a potential slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods when HOUST < 1300.0 and the economy is in a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a key indicator of labor market health; higher unemployment signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of the periods.
